text:
pagerduty-bot: PD Alert: synthetic-watchdog-eu-west triggered (INC-2026). multiple failing probes, current severity: P2. page fired to oncall

eli: acked. oncall taking it. seeing PD note about probe backlog + repeated failures.

eli: quick check — dashboards show probe failure rate spiking from 0.2% -> 12% over last 3m in eu-west-1. latency of the probe runner also up. not yet seeing app errors in prod metrics.

sre-bot: automatic action: added suppress-window for 5m to reduce duplicate pages.

maria: thanks. eli, can you confirm whether this is limited to synthetic runner or also affects user-facing inference endpoints?

eli: running quick query: `sum(rate(infra_synth_failures_total{region=\"eu-west-1\"}[5m])) by (probe_type)` shows spike on `http-liveness` and `tls-handshake` probes. `redwood_api_5xx` is flat. so likely synthetic infra or network path between prober fleet and endpoints.

sam: paging notes — PD shows two unacked pages in the last 2m before suppression. PD auto-escalated to ops-lead, then to platform. looks like a noisy fanout of identical failures.

jordan: posting probe logs from a runner node (anonymized):
```
2026-03-15T02:44:10Z synth-runner[pid=1987]: probe=eu-west-1 target=api-eu.prod.redwood.ai status=503 body=\"upstream reset by peer\"
2026-03-15T02:44:11Z synth-runner[pid=1987]: probe=eu-west-1 target=api-eu.prod.redwood.ai error=tls: handshake failure
2026-03-15T02:44:12Z synth-runner[pid=1987]: probe=eu-west-1 target=cached-edge-eu status=200 latency=134ms
```

eli: interesting — some targets return 200 while others 503/tls fail. could be specific edge pool or service routing.

maria: do we have any config changes or cert rotations around 02:40 UTC?

eli: config deploys: none in last hour. cert rotation job shows a successful run at 01:50 UTC. nothing near spike.

sam: I'm going to put prober into degraded mode to stop paging while we triage: `/synthctl set-mode eu-west-1 degraded --suppress-pager` (will still collect traces).

oncall-bot: command accepted by synthctl. setting mode=degraded for region eu-west-1. note: degraded will lower probe concurrency and suppress pages for 10m.

eli: after degraded mode, paging should stop; we still need to investigate root cause. running `kubectl -n synth get pods -l app=synth-runner -o wide` now.

jordan: kubectl output (trimmed):
```
NAME                                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
synth-runner-5f8c7d9b6c-2k9qv           1/1     Running   0          12d   i-0a1b2c3d
synth-runner-5f8c7d9b6c-7lpkd           1/1     Running   1          12d   i-0f9e8d7c
synth-runner-5f8c7d9b6c-9xv2r           0/1     CrashLoop  4          3h    i-0b2c3d4e
```

eli: there's a runner in CrashLoop on node i-0b2c3d4e — looks correlated. pulling logs from that pod now.

jordan: pod logs snippet:
```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
goroutine 42 [running]:
  github.com/redwood/synth-runner/prober.(*Runner).doProbe(0xc000114000, 0x...)\n  /go/src/.../prober/runner.go:212 +0x2a3
```

maria: Aha - suspicious. CrashLoop started ~3h ago but error rate only spiking now because fanout increased? any recent traffic changes?

eli: fanout spike? yes, we increased synthetic concurrency for eu to 50 -> 200 probes per minute at 02:40 in an AB run to improve coverage. that lines up. the crashed pod likely got overloaded and is now flapping causing some probes to fail TLS or return 503s.

sam: mitigation plan: 1) scale down synth-runner deployment concurrency to previous levels; 2) cordon the bad node and drain; 3) restart crashed pods after image debug build; 4) re-enable normal probe rate when stable. I'll run the scale now: `kubectl -n synth scale deploy/synth-runner --replicas=3`

oncall-bot: scaling command issued by sam. desired replicas=3.

eli: I'm going to cordon i-0b2c3d4e and drain; suspect underlying VM had IO pressure causing TLS failures.

jordan: cordon/drain done. pods rescheduled. new pods look healthy: `synth-runner-...-abcde READY 1/1`.

sre-bot: Notice: probe failure rate dropped from 12% -> 0.7% over next 4m after scale/down/fix.

maria: good. customer impact assessment: no increase in user 5xx or latency in API metrics. likely internal synthetic-only. still, PD noise was excessive — we should tweak alerting thresholds and add rate-limiting on fanout changes.

eli: agreed. follow-ups: - roll a hotfix to make runner more resilient to corrupted TLS state (issue created: GH#synth-789) - add circuit-breaker to prevent single node CrashLoop from affecting whole fanout - add canary for probe concurrency changes so we ramp more slowly

sam: logging follow-up: capture core dumps from crashed pod and attach to GH issue. tagging infra/edge to audit node IO at time window.

maria: handing off to next oncall for long-running follow-ups. summary: synthetic concurrency AB run caused a prober CrashLoop on one node -> local TLS/503 failures -> noisy pages. mitigated by degraded-mode, scale down, cordon+drain. no customer-facing impact. follow-up GH items created.

eli: taking note — handing to maria for postmortem. maria, you want to own the follow-ups?

maria: I will own follow-ups. taking handoff. ack.

oncall-bot: handoff recorded: from eli to maria at 2026-03-15T03:01:45Z. incident status: mitigated, monitoring.

sam: closing PD incident if no further regressions in 15m.

pagerduty-bot: PD Update: INC-2026 auto-resolved by user action (suppress + scale) at 2026-03-15T03:10:02Z.

eli: thanks team. will draft a short writeup for postmortem and link GH#synth-789. :thumbsup:
